paper.citation: Vaswani, A., Shazeer, N., Parmar, N., Uszkoreit, J., Jones, L., Gomez, A.N., Kaiser, L., Polosukhin, I. (2017). Attention Is All You Need. NIPS 2017. arXiv:1706.03762v7

constraints.audience: graduate ML seminar, familiar with seq2seq basics

speaker_notes.value: in-pptx notes slides (see slide_evidence_map notes field)

value.claim: The Transformer removes recurrence and convolutions from sequence transduction using attention only.

evidence.quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

value.claim: RNN-based transduction is fundamentally sequential, so training cannot be parallelized within a sequence.

evidence.quote: Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences.
The fundamental constraint of sequential computation, however, remains.

value.claim: Core idea: keep only attention - self-attention replaces recurrence everywhere, at a fraction of the training cost.

evidence.quote: these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train
we use h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads

value.claim: The architecture: 6-layer encoder (left) and decoder (right) built from multi-head self-attention + position-wise FFN sub-layers.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.
evidence.supports: architecture diagram, original figure from the paper

evidence.quote: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.

value.claim: Scaled dot-product attention is computed per head, then concatenated; complexity per layer is O(n^2 * d) but constant in path length.

evidence.quote: We suspect that for large values of dk, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients
Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
Maximum path lengths, per-layer complexity and minimum number of sequential operations

value.claim: Training recipe: Adam with warmup-then-decay schedule, heavy regularization (dropout 0.1, label smoothing 0.1).

evidence.quote: We used the Adam optimizer [20] with β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.98 and ε = 10−9.
We employ three types of regularization during training: resid[ual] drop[out] ... label smoothing
evidence.supports: note: quote lightly normalized from line-wrapped PDF text

value.claim: Headline results: 28.4 BLEU EN-DE (>2 BLEU over previous best including ensembles) and 41.8 BLEU EN-FR single-model SOTA, at a fraction of training FLOPs.

evidence.quote: The Transformer achieves better BLEU scores than previous state-of-the-art models on the English-to-German and English-to-French newstest2014 tests at a fraction of the training cost.
evidence.supports: headline table; numbers above read from Table 2 rows

evidence.quote: improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU

value.claim: The architecture generalizes beyond translation: strong English constituency parsing results with both large and limited training data.

evidence.quote: The Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing
evidence.supports: parsing results table (caption paraphrased from abstract sentence)

evidence.quote: We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.

value.claim: Takeaways: attention-only transduction is faster to train and stronger; the paper itself lists no explicit limitations, so the caveats below are the presenter's reading.

evidence.quote: we presented the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention
We plan to extend the Transformer to problems involving input and output modalities other than text
evidence.supports: future work only - the caveat bullets are the presenter's interpretation, flagged in-slide

problem.statement: Dominant sequence transduction models (RNN/LSTM encoder-decoder with attention) compute sequentially along symbol positions, blocking parallelization within a training sequence and making training slow.

evidence.quote: Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences.
The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder.

method.statement: The Transformer: an encoder-decoder built solely on attention (multi-head self-attention + point-wise FFN), no recurrence or convolution, with positional encodings injecting order.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.
The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.
we use h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads

results.statement: 28.4 BLEU on WMT14 EN-DE (over 2 BLEU above previous best including ensembles) and 41.8 BLEU on WMT14 EN-FR (new single-model SOTA) at a fraction of the training cost; also generalizes to English constituency parsing.

evidence.quote: The Transformer achieves better BLEU scores than previous state-of-the-art models on the English-to-German and English-to-French newstest2014 tests at a fraction of the training cost.
our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs

limitations.statement: The paper has no explicit limitations section. Inferred caveats: results shown on translation + one parsing task only; the fixed learned positional encoding targets sequences up to a maximum length; the paper does not study data efficiency below large corpora.

evidence.quote: We plan to extend the Transformer to problems involving input and output modalities other than text
evidence.note: future-work phrasing only; no limitations section exists in the paper

evidence.quote: we also inject information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence
evidence.note: positional encoding is length-bound (inference by the deck author, flagged)

limitations.uncertainty_flag: limitation statements 2 and 3 are the presenter's interpretation, not verbatim paper claims
